claims.claim: Microsoft Xbox One S All-Digital Edition Console (disc-free).
claims.evidence: Witness photos show a large rectangular electronics-looking item wrapped in clear plastic with a fine metal mesh front; no console shape, disc-drive absence, or Xbox branding/model label is readable.

claims.claim: Neatly used, never opened or repaired.
claims.evidence: Photos do not show seals, opening marks, or internal condition; no serial/inspection evidence is visible.
Photos cannot confirm overheating history; no temperature/usage logs or test results are shown.
No ports/connectors are visible in the provided angles; no functional test is shown.

claims.claim: Comes with the original pads and the UK receipt.
claims.evidence: No accessories or receipt are shown in the witness photos.

risks.risk: Item may not be an Xbox console at all (photos look like a mesh-front speaker/audio cabinet panel rather than a game console).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the front and back of the device showing Xbox One S ports/labels (HDMI, power, USB) and the Xbox logo/model text, with the item unwrapped enough to read the nameplate.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a non-identified mesh-front electronics item (worst case: not the claimed console), i.e., treat as lower-value/unknown for parts or resale until identity is confirmed.

risks.risk: If it is an Xbox, it may be the wrong variant (not actually All-Digital Edition) or wrong model generation.
risks.proof: Photo of the model/serial label (sticker) and a shot of the front panel area showing disc slot presence/absence (or the exact model text).
risks.if_unproven: Price as the least certain/lowest-spec variant (worst case: not the claimed All-Digital Edition) until the label/model is readable.

risks.risk: Port failure or non-working components (seller claims all ports work, but no test is shown).
risks.proof: Short video clip showing the console powered on and a functional check: HDMI display output, at least one USB device recognized, and controller pairing; include a quick port-by-port plug/unplug demonstration.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not fully tested / potentially faulty electronics (worst case: needs repair), reflecting uncertainty.

risks.risk: Overheating/thermal issues or prior damage not visible externally.
risks.proof: Video clip of a short stress/usage test (e.g., boot into dashboard and run a game/menu for several minutes) with no shutdowns, plus a photo of vents/thermal condition.
risks.if_unproven: Price as potential thermal fault risk (worst case: may overheat), until a live test is provided.

risks.risk: Accessories/receipt may be missing or not original.
risks.proof: Photos of all included items laid out (pads/controllers, cables, receipt/UK proof) with matching serial/model where applicable.
risks.if_unproven: Price without assumed accessories/receipt (worst case: only the main unit), until items are shown.

proof_requests: Unwrap and photograph the exact front and back of the device showing Xbox branding, port layout, and any model/serial label (readable).
Provide a clear close-up of the model/serial sticker (or a screenshot of the console system info if it powers on).
Send a short power-on video showing the console booting to the dashboard (or equivalent) and confirming it is disc-free (no disc slot).
Show a quick functional port test: HDMI output on a TV/monitor, USB recognition, and controller pairing.
Show photos of included accessories (pads/controllers, cables) and the UK receipt.
response.reason: The witness photos do not provide enough visual evidence to confirm the item is an Xbox One S All-Digital Edition; the visible mesh-front wrapped object could be something else. Without identity and a basic power/port test, any pricing would be too risky.
